video_title_guess: The Road Trippin' Show: Wembanyama's Elbow and Defensive Dominance

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: Let's establish this now. He has taken over the throne of being the most dominant player in the NBA. He snatched that from Giannis. However you want to look at it, the most dominant player could go two ways. He's definitely the most dominant player I've seen with my own two eyes defensively. Hands down. Opponents are doing U-turns driving to the paint. And sometimes he's not even in the game. But they forget just the thought. He'd already played mind games with these people.
quotes.why_it_matters: Kendrick Perkins boldly declares Victor Wembanyama the most dominant player in the NBA, especially defensively, noting his psychological impact on opponents who alter their play even when he's not on the court.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: We're here for views, we're here for viewership and stardom over somebody's health, to the expense of Naz Reid. Forget how his jaw and neck feel at the moment. He seemed fine. Yeah, forget how his jaw feels, right? You are on that side of the fence. Forget how his jaw feels. Forget how his family members feel. If he has kids, forget how they feel watching his daddy get elbowed all in the throat like this UFC.
quotes.why_it_matters: Kendrick Perkins controversially prioritizes Victor Wembanyama's stardom and league viewership over Naz Reid's physical well-being after the elbow incident, sarcastically dismissing concerns for Reid's injury and family.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: Here's the real question. Where is a goon for the Spurs? Wemby is your centerpiece of your team. He is getting beat up. He is getting elbowed, grabbed, pushed, thrown to the ground. Somebody has to stick up for your best player. One person has to stick up for Wemby so that he doesn't have to do it. Wemby, don't worry about it, bro. I got you. Come on, send him right here. Elbow to the chest, foul, boom. Don't worry about it, Wemby.
quotes.why_it_matters: Channing Frye criticizes the Spurs' lack of a physical enforcer to protect Victor Wembanyama, suggesting the team needs to step up to prevent their star from having to retaliate himself.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: If you watch, obviously I'm on the Twitter sphere a lot. They showed the last 15 clips of Wemby either getting pushed, elbowed, tripped. At a certain point, my guy, Wemby, good for you. Sometimes you have to knock a motherfucker's head off. You just have to. That was a clean ass elbow, all that Shaolin stuff finally came into fruition. He straight elbowed. Was it right? Absolutely not. But he has to defend himself.
quotes.why_it_matters: Channing Frye argues Wembanyama's elbow was a justified response to repeated physical play, highlighting the need for players to defend themselves on the court.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: I get it, man, but Wemby, this is just the appetizer of what you're going to get. When you get the full entree the rest of your career, guys are going to play you physical. Channing, if I was playing against Wemby, my thing would be to frustrate him. Yes, every now and then, I may hit him with a little chicken wing in his ribs. Every now and then, when he goes up for a layup, it might be a borderline flagrant around the shoulders type stuff. It is what it is, bro. You can't stop him.
quotes.why_it_matters: Kendrick Perkins advises Victor Wembanyama to prepare for consistent physical play throughout his career, stating that opponents will try to frustrate him with borderline fouls because he is unstoppable.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: I have never in my life seen a defensive player like Victor Wembanyama. This guy could block a shot and take away the drop-off pass from the big at the same time while he's in the air. I'll block it with the right and I have this other long arm ready for a deflection. There's nothing you could do when you drive to the paint on him. It is, I've never seen dominance of this level. Ally, Channing, am I saying something crazy here?
quotes.why_it_matters: Kendrick Perkins marvels at Victor Wembanyama's unprecedented defensive abilities, highlighting his unique skill to simultaneously block shots and disrupt passing lanes, making him an impenetrable force in the paint.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: No, no, no. He's doing things that we will never see again because I played against tall guys. His versatility, his defensive presence, his ability to, you say, hey, we're going to play this two-on-two. You could play it two-on-one. Wemby's like, you're not going to shoot that layup and you're also not going to throw this lob. You can't really shoot the jumper because I'm not even trying to block it in your hand. I'm blocking it in the air. So all these things, he's shutting off sections, he might as well be the water main because he's shutting off sections of the basketball court. No, you just go play over there on that side of the court.
quotes.why_it_matters: Channing Frye emphasizes Victor Wembanyama's unparalleled defensive versatility and presence, describing how he effectively shuts down entire sections of the court, forcing opponents to completely alter their offensive strategies.
